chain: Less GH-driven bone and soft-tissue growth
pegvisomant.text: Pegvisomant is discussed in appearance circles as the opposite of a growth hormone booster: it lowers IGF-1 and is used in acromegaly, where excess GH enlarges the jaw, brow and hands. Its cosmetic relevance is as a reference point for GH-driven facial change; it has not been studied for cosmetic use.

bivamelagon.text: Bivamelagon is an oral MC4R agonist that fat-loss followers watch as a possible appetite-control route to a leaner look. It is being studied for weight gain after hypothalamic damage; no data exist in cosmetic or general fat-loss use.

rm-718.text: RM-718 is a weekly MC4R agonist followed by fat-loss researchers as a possible route to appetite control and a leaner physique. It is in early trials for rare obesity syndromes, and no results or cosmetic data are available.

pl-8177.text: PL-8177 is an MC1r agonist that tanning-peptide readers connect to melanocortin-driven pigmentation and a deeper tan. It has been studied in inflammatory bowel and eye models rather than for tanning, so the appearance link is untested.

chain: Alters appetite signalling in lab models
shu-9119.text: SHU-9119 is a melanocortin antagonist used in rodent studies as a tool to block appetite-regulating signalling, which is how it enters fat-loss discussions. It has no human studies, and its appearance relevance is as a research reference for melanocortin agonists.

s-23.text: S-23 is a SARM sold as a research chemical, and users take it hoping for muscle gain with fewer steroid-like effects, building a more muscular physique. It was developed as a male contraceptive candidate; its muscle effects are based on animal work and anecdote, with no published human trials.

chain: Anabolic effect on muscle and bone
s-40503.text: S-40503 is a SARM noted in muscle-building circles for its tissue-selective androgen receptor activity, which is linked to lean mass gain. It was studied in rat osteoporosis models and is known mostly from doping-control research; there are no human efficacy data.

chain: Anabolic effect on muscle and bone
lgd-2226.text: LGD-2226 is a SARM that users take hoping to add muscle with less prostate stimulation than testosterone. Animal studies showed anabolic effects on muscle and bone; there are no human trials, and it is sold as a research chemical.

lgd-2941.text: LGD-2941 is a quinolinone SARM that muscle-building communities treat as a lean mass candidate. It was investigated for cachexia and hypogonadism, then discontinued after Phase I, so its appearance use rests on almost no public data.

chain: Anabolic effect in muscle and bone
lgd-3303.text: LGD-3303 is an oral SARM discussed by people seeking muscle gain through selective androgen receptor activity. Published work covers only animal and in vitro studies in rats and horses; human muscle effects are untested.

acp-105.text: ACP-105 is a partial-agonist SARM that users take hoping for lean mass gain with milder androgenic effects. It improved anabolic markers in castrated rats and mice; there are no human trials, and it is sold online as a research chemical.

ac-262536.text: AC-262,536 is a SARM that users take in pursuit of lean muscle gain. It improved anabolic parameters in castrated rats in a two-week study; human muscle effects are untested, and it is sold as a research chemical.

bms-564929.text: BMS-564929 is a highly potent SARM mentioned by muscle-building users for its strong muscle effect with little prostate stimulation in rats. It was developed for age-related decline and stalled in early trials, so its use for physique rests on rat data.

glpg0492.text: GLPG0492 is a non-steroidal SARM that users take hoping to build muscle with weaker effects on the prostate. It was tested in mouse muscle-wasting models and phase 1 volunteer trials; efficacy in people is not shown.

chain: Favors muscle and bone in rats
tfm-4as-1.text: TFM-4AS-1 is a steroidal SARM that muscle-building readers cite for favoring muscle and bone over reproductive tissue in rats. It has never been tested in people, so its physique use rests on laboratory work.

mk-0773.text: MK-0773 is a steroidal SARM tested for sarcopenia, where it added lean mass in frail older women. It did not improve strength or function in that phase 2 trial, and users interested in physique follow it as a human-data example.

chain: Gain in lean mass and leg strength
gsk2881078.text: GSK2881078 is a SARM that raised lean mass in older adults and leg strength in men with COPD, so muscle-focused readers cite it as one of the better human data sets. Trials were in ill or older people, not people seeking a cosmetic physique.

opk-88004.text: OPK-88004 is a SARM that raised lean mass and reduced fat in prostate cancer survivors, which is the body-composition change followers of SARMs look for. Symptoms and performance did not improve in that trial, and it has not been studied for appearance.

mk-3984.text: MK-3984 is an obscure SARM that muscle-building communities occasionally list as a lean-mass candidate. Little is published beyond a doping-control metabolite study in zebrafish, and there are no human data.

arcarine.text: Arcarine (ORM-11984) is a SARM from Orion that muscle-building readers know as a discontinued candidate for selective muscle activation. It reached Phase I and left almost no public data on muscle or appearance.

gsk-971086.text: GSK-971086 is an indole-class SARM that was investigated for sarcopenia and androgen deficiency, and is followed by muscle-building readers as a lean-mass candidate. It never got past Phase I, and no efficacy data exist.

gsk-2849466.text: GSK-2849466 is a SARM that was investigated for cachexia and heart failure, and muscle-focused readers note it as a lean-mass candidate. Development stopped after one small Phase I trial, so appearance effects are untested.

gtx-027.text: GTx-027 is a SARM explored for breast cancer and stress urinary incontinence, and is occasionally listed by muscle-building readers among SARMs. It is essentially preclinical, with no data on muscle or appearance.

ly305.text: LY305 is a SARM built as a transdermal treatment for low testosterone, which makes it of interest to those seeking a muscle and hormone-related physique. It was also explored for muscle wasting; there are no appearance data.

pf-06260414.text: PF-06260414 is Pfizer's oral SARM, studied for cachexia and tested for safety in healthy men. It was shelved after Phase I, and muscle-building readers follow it only as a candidate without appearance data.

jnj-26146900.text: JNJ-26146900 is a SARM investigated for prostate cancer and noted by muscle-building readers for its androgen receptor selectivity. It was tested only in rats and never in humans, so its appearance use is untested.

ru-59063.text: RU-59063 is a 1990s research androgen-receptor ligand, sometimes classed as a SARM, and became a template for later antiandrogens. It has no human use, and its appearance link in muscle circles is theoretical.

bolandiol.text: Bolandiol is a nandrolone-related steroid with mixed androgen, estrogen and progestin activity, discussed by physique-focused readers as an anabolic. It was studied in rats and never marketed as a base; human appearance data are lacking.

dienolone.text: Dienolone is a nandrolone-like steroid that physique readers mention for its anabolic class. It was developed as RU-3118 and never marketed, and is mainly of interest as a chemical intermediate; human muscle effects are untested.

norclostebol.text: Norclostebol is a chlorinated nandrolone derivative described in 1957 and mentioned by physique readers for its anabolic class. It has no listed medical use and no human studies of muscle or appearance.
